paper.title: Cooperative Online Learning with Feedback Graphs

settings.name_in_paper: Cooperative online learning with feedback graphs (stochastic agent activations, oblivious network interface)
unmapped: Network of agents on an undirected communication graph N; each agent is activated independently each round with probability q(v); Q = sum_v q(v)
Messages travel along N with delay equal to shortest-path distance, up to diffusion radius n
Regret is network regret summed over active agents
Each agent knows q(u) for agents within distance n but not the global network topology (oblivious network interface)
settings.definition_quote:
An instance of our problem is parameterized by:
\begin{enumerate}[topsep=0pt,parsep=0pt,itemsep=0pt]
    \item A \textbf{communication network} $\Gnet = (\Vnet,\Enet)$ over a set $\Vnet$ of agents, and a {maximum communication delay} $\dnet\ge 0$, limiting the communication among agents.
    \item A \textbf{feedback graph} $\Gfeed = (\Vfeed, \Efeed)$ over a set $\Vfeed$ of actions.
    \item An \textbf{activation probability} $q(v)>0$ for each agent $v\in \Vnet$,

settings.name_in_paper: Cooperative online learning with feedback graphs (lower bound)
unmapped: Network of agents with independent stochastic activations q(v), Q = sum q(v); network regret over active agents
Communication delay equal to graph distance, diffusion radius n
Activation probabilities chosen adversarially subject to sum Q
settings.definition_quote: the supremum is over all assignments of losses $\ell = (\ell_t)_{t\in [T]}$ and activation probabilities $\brb{ q(v) }_{v\in\Vnet}$ such that $Q=\sum_{v\in\Vnet}q(v)$.

settings.name_in_paper: Single-agent online learning with feedback graph and randomly skipped rounds (lower bound)
unmapped: Each round is independently active with known constant probability mu (Bernoulli A_t); inactive rounds incur no loss, give no feedback, and do not count toward regret
settings.definition_quote: at each round t, there is an independent Bernoulli random variable A_t with mean mu. If A_t=0, the learner is not required to make any predictions, incurs no loss, and receives no feedback information.

symbols.Q: expected number of active agents per round, sum_v q(v)
symbols.n_rad: diffusion radius / maximum communication delay n
symbols.alpha_NF: independence number of the strong product N^n ⊠ F of the n-th power of the communication network and the feedback graph

conditions: agents run with an oblivious network interface
each agent knows q(u) for agents within distance n
tuning: eta_t(v)=0 for t<=n+1, eta_t(v)=sqrt(log K / sum_{s<=t} X_s(v)) with X_t(v)= n + sum_i p_t(i,v)/b_t(i,v)

source.label: t:upper

results.notes: Theorem bounds average regret R_T/Q; multiplied by Q to give total network regret. Proof gives explicit R_T <= Q(n+1) + 3Q sqrt(log K (n+1+alpha/(Q(1-1/e))) T). Regret defined as max over i of expected difference with oblivious losses (pseudo-regret). Adaptive learning rates: no knowledge of T, alpha, Q needed.

symbols.mu: probability that each round is active (A_t ~ Bernoulli(mu))

source.label: l:lower
source.quote:
For any feedback graph $\Gfeed$,
\changes{for any (possibly randomized) online learning algorithm \alg,}
for any $\changes{\mu} > 0$, and for any $T\ge\max\bcb{0.0064 \cdot \alpha(\Gfeed)^3,\frac{1}{\changes{\mu}^{3}}}$,

if each round $t \in [T]$ is independently skipped with probability $\changes{\mu}$, then

\[
    \inf_{\alg}\sup_{\ell} \Rsingle_{T}(\changes{\mu},\alg,\ell) \overset{\Omega}{=} \sqrt{\alpha(\Gfeed)\changes{\mu}T}~.
\]

results.notes: Proof yields explicit constant 3/4. Text says 'skipped with probability mu' but the formal model has rounds active with probability mu (A_t has mean mu).

symbols.Q: total activation mass sum_v q(v), Q in (0, alpha(N^n)]
symbols.alpha_F: independence number of the feedback graph F
symbols.alpha_N: independence number of the communication network (paper writes alpha(N), proof uses alpha(N^n))

conditions: (N^n, F) in class G: alpha(N^n ⊠ F) = alpha(N^n) alpha(F)
algorithm run with an oblivious network interface (each agent runs an instance of the same algorithm)
supremum over losses and activation probabilities q with sum q(v) = Q

source.label: t:lower
source.quote:
For any choice of $n$, any pair of graphs $(\Gnet^n,\Gfeed) \in \mathscr{G}$, and all $Q\in (0,\alphanet]$, we have that for  $T\geq\max\left\{0.0064 \cdot \alpha(\Gfeed)^{3},\alpha(\Gnet)^{3}/Q^3\right\}$ the following holds
\[
    \inf_{\changes{\alg}} \sup_{\ell,q} R_T(q,\changes{\alg},\ell) \overset{\Omega}{=} \sqrt{Q \alpha\big(\Gnet^{\dnet} \boxtimes \Gfeed\big) T } \;,
\]
where

\changes{the infimum is over all randomized online algorithms} and the supremum is over all assignments of losses $\ell = (\ell_t)_{t\in [T]}$ and activation probabilities $\brb{ q(v) }_{v\in\Vnet}$ such that $Q=\sum_{v\in\Vnet}q(v)$.

results.notes: Instance-dependent in the graph pair (N,F); worst case over losses and activations. R_T(q,alg,l) defined as network regret of alg run with oblivious network interface.
